company_description: FactSet Research Systems Inc., together with its subsidiaries, operates as a financial digital platform and enterprise solutions provider for the investment community. It offers data, products, and analytical applications; and workstations, portfolio analytics, and enterprise data solutions, as well as managed services for supporting data, performance, risk, and reporting workflows. The company also provides subscription-based financial data and market intelligence on securities, companies, industries, and people that enable clients to research investment ideas, as well as analyze, monitor, and manage portfolios; and solutions covering investment lifecycle of investment research, portfolio construction and analysis, trade execution, performance measurement, risk management, and reporting. In addition, it offers services through configurable desktop and mobile platform, data feeds, cloud-based digital solutions, and application programming interfaces. It operates in Europe, the Middle East, Africa, the Americas, the Asia Pacific, and internationally. risks.title: Dependence on Subscriptions and Customer Cancellations
risks.summary: The company relies heavily on subscription revenues. An increase in customer cancellations, despite high retention rates, could affect recurring revenue growth.
risks.score_rationale: The text states that revenues are primarily subscription-based and that customers can add, remove, or cancel services. Higher customer churn could negatively impact recurring revenues (ASV).

risks.title: Integration and Costs of Acquisitions
risks.summary: The company's growth is partly driven by acquisitions. Integrating new entities and managing associated costs pose a potential risk to profitability.
risks.score_rationale: The text notes that revenue and employee growth are partially due to acquisitions (Irwin, Liquid Holdings). Successful integration and cost management are critical for future performance.

risks.title: Rising Service Costs
risks.summary: Service costs, particularly amortization of intangible assets and personnel compensation, are increasing faster than revenues, which could erode operating margins.
risks.score_rationale: Service costs increased by 8.5%, outpacing revenue growth (5.4%). Higher amortization of intangible assets and personnel costs are pressuring margins.

risks.title: Increased Competition in Financial Data Market
risks.summary: The financial platform sector is highly competitive. The company must continuously innovate to maintain its position against existing and new players.
risks.score_rationale: Although not explicitly detailed in this excerpt, the financial platform market is inherently competitive. The need to innovate and maintain an attractive offering is constant.

risks.title: Tax Dispute-Related Risks
risks.summary: The company incurred significant charges from a tax dispute. Although the impact appears to have diminished, future disputes or changing tax regulations could affect financials.
risks.score_rationale: The text mentions charges related to a 'Sales Tax Dispute' in the prior year, which had a significant impact on SG&A. While resolved or ongoing, similar future disputes could arise.

risks.title: Dependence on Workforce Growth in Centers of Excellence
risks.summary: A significant concentration of employees in overseas centers of excellence creates dependency. Disruptions in these regions or recruitment challenges could impact operations.
risks.score_rationale: A large portion of the workforce (68%) is concentrated in centers of excellence (Philippines, India). Disruptions in these regions or difficulties attracting/retaining talent could impact operations.

risks.title: Foreign Exchange Rate Fluctuations
risks.summary: Currency exchange rate fluctuations can have an impact, even if currently limited, on the consolidated revenues of the company operating internationally.
risks.score_rationale: The text notes the impact of exchange rate fluctuations on revenues (0.1% in 2025). While currently low, increased volatility could have a more significant effect.
